items.text: In the northern Philippines, a long-lasting drought has caused a dam to shrink, unveiling the ruins of a centuries-old town. This newfound sight has become an attraction for locals. Also, it serves as an additional source of income in an area reliant on rice cultivation . The dried-up dam has exposed parts of an ancient church and the foundations of other old buildings in Nueva Ecija province. Residents like Aurea Delos Santos, a retired nurse, express excitement at the sight’s revelation. Some locals, like fisherman Nelson Dellera, have taken the opportunity to profit by taking tourists to the site. The old town had been relocated in the 1970s during the dam’s construction. The dam now plays a crucial role in providing irrigation and water to the region; however, extreme heat in the Philippines and neighboring countries has led to various challenges, including suspended school classes. Difficult words: unveil (to reveal), cultivation (preparing the land and growing crops on it), irrigation (supplying water to land or crops to help growth). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

It was very hot in the northern Philippines recently, which caused a dam in the Nueva Ecija region to shrink . Workers built the dam in the 1970s, but they had to move a town and people who lived in it. As the dam dried up, ruins of the town emerged . This new sight is very popular not only with local people but many tourists come to see it, too. They can see parts of an old church and other old buildings. The area depends on rice farming, and local people welcome the chance to make extra money. Some people, like fisherman Nelson Dellera, make money by taking tourists to the ruins. The dam provides water for the whole area and farmers depend on it. But big heat in the Philippines and neighboring countries is causing problems. Farmers have little water, officials cancel school classes and they ask people to stay indoors. Difficult words: dam (a high wall across a river which collects water), shrink (to become smaller), emerge (to become visible). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

It does not rain for a long time in the Philippines. In the north of the country, there is a dam . Now, the dam gets smaller. There is not enough water in it. In the 1970s, workers build the dam. There is a town. They move the town and its people away. Now, the water is away. People can see the ruins of the town. There is an old church and other buildings. People there are happy. They can see this old place and get more money from visitors. Most people live from farming there. Now, they bring tourists to the town. Many farmers grow rice in the Philippines. They need water. Now, they have problems. Neighboring countries have problems too. It is too hot for too long. Schools close in the Philippines. People must stay inside. Difficult words: dam (a high wall across a river which collects water), church (a building where Christians speak to god), neighboring (a country which is next to another country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Renowned French actor Gerard Depardieu faces trial in October for alleged sexual assaults on a 2021 film set. Depardieu, a prominent figure in French cinema, has faced increasing sexual assault accusations in recent years, which damaged his reputation and sparked debates about sexual conduct in France. Police have questioned the actor; however, Depardieu denies any wrongdoing and has been released without charge. Moreover, he faces another indictment for a separate alleged sexual assault and rape case from August 2018, which is now under investigation by the Paris public prosecutor. These allegations have divided society in France. Some support Depardieu as a talented actor, while others view his case as emblematic of broader issues around sexual abuse and power dynamics in the country. Difficult words: alleged (said without proof), prominent (important and well-known), indictment (formal charge), emblematic (symbolic). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

French actor Gerard Depardieu will go to court in October. The reason is alleged sexual attacks during making a film in 2021. Depardieu is a famous movie star in France, and this problem divides French people. Some people believe that he did nothing wrong but others say that this points to a much bigger problem in the country. The case hurt the actor’s reputation and started talks about sexual behavior in the country. Depardieu keeps saying that he did nothing wrong. Police are also looking into another case of Depardieu’s sexual attack in 2018. Difficult words: alleged (possible), reputation (what many people think about someone or something), behavior (how someone acts). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Gerard Depardieu is a French actor. He is very famous . Many people like him very much. But the man has problems. He will go to court in October. Some women say that he hurts them. It happens when he is making a movie in 2021. The actor keeps saying that he does nothing wrong. But police are checking another similar problem from 2018. The problem divides people in France. Some people believe the man. They say that he is a great man. Other people say that the problem with sexual attacks in France is much bigger. Difficult words: famous (when many people know someone), divide (separate into parts), sexual attack (when a person wants to have sex with someone but they do not agree). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Despite their popularity, political polls often seen on TV during elections, sometimes give inaccurate results, and some Americans question their trustworthiness. In both 2016 and 2020, most national polls overestimated support for Democrats. Polls aim to show what people think at a certain time but can be tricky to predict future outcomes accurately. Mallory Newall explains that reliable polls focus on understanding public opinions rather than just predicting election winners. She warns against reading too much into small differences in polls, especially far from election day. Red flags for bad polls include not representing the right people and not being clear about how the data was collected. Polling methods have changed since 2016, with more surveys done online. Online surveys may influence results; however, concerns remain about reaching everyone, especially in rural areas without good internet. Although there are challenges, polls remain important for understanding public opinion. Difficult words: overestimate (to guess an amount that is too high or a size that is too big), outcome (the way a thing turns out), red flag (a sign that something bad is happening or could happen). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Polls try to show and help understand what people think, especially during elections. But sometimes they are not right, because it is hard to guess the future. Polls on TV sometimes get things wrong. In 2016 and 2020, they said that more Americans would vote for Democrats than actually did. Good pools try to understand people and their opinions, rather than just guess who will win. Small differences in polls aren’t always important, but polling methods must be transparent. It must be clear how they got their information. Polls changed since 2016. There are more online polls, but there are problems like no response or bad internet access in villages. Although is it not easy to guess the result, polls are still important for understanding what people think. Difficult words: guess (when you give an answer but you are not sure that you are correct), method (the way of doing something), response (an answer). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Polls tell us what people think. Political polls before elections tell us who could be the winner. But TV polls sometimes get things wrong. In 2016 and 2020, they say that more Americans will vote for Democrats. But that does not happen. Guessing the future is hard. Good polls want to understand people, not only guess. Sometimes it is not clear where the information comes from. Since 2016, polls are different. More polls are online. But some people cannot do these polls, for example in places without good internet. Polls are not always accurate . But they are important. They tell us what people think. Difficult words: elections (when people choose a person in politics), guess (when you say something but you are not sure that you are right), accurate (correct, right). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Kenya’s president William Ruto has announced evacuation plans for areas at risk of flooding or landslides following severe flooding that claimed at least 169 lives. The Army is mobilized to help with evacuations, especially in the Rift Valley, north of Nairobi, where an overflowing reservoir wiped out houses and caused significant casualties . Rescue teams, including the Red Cross and National Youth Service, are using bulldozers to clear debris and they are searching for bodies along riverbanks. Despite criticism, the president defends the government’s response and he assures that emergency plans are in place. The government is considering declaring a national disaster; however, the immediate focus remains on providing aid and coordinating emergency responses. Difficult words: mobilized (organized and sent out for action), casualty (a person killed or injured in a war or accident). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Severe floods killed at least 169 people in Kenya. Kenya’s president William Ruto said that people in flood- prone areas should leave their homes. The Army is helping move people away, especially in the Rift Valley, north of the capital Nairobi. A full reservoir broke there, destroyed part of a village, and killed 48 people. Rescue teams are using bulldozers to clear debris . They are searching for bodies along rivers. Some people criticize the government’s slow response, but the president said that everyone did what they could. Rescue teams, including the Red Cross, are in place. The government may declare a national disaster later, but now they focus on helping people. Difficult words: prone (to be likely to suffer from something), debris (pieces of rubbish or other things), declare (to say something clearly and in public). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Kenya, floods kill at least 170 people. The president says that people in some places must leave their homes. There is more rain coming. It is dangerous to stay. The Army is helping people leave. In the Rift Valley, north of Nairobi, a lot of water destroys part of a village . Many people die there. Rescue teams are looking for bodies near rivers. They are clearing trees and stuff from the water. The government is getting ready to help more. They may say that it is a national disaster . But for now, they are just trying to make everyone safe. Difficult words: flood (too much water in rivers, streets and so on), village (a group of houses and other buildings which is smaller than a tows), national disaster (a very bad event which has an impact on the whole country). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

For decades, people have worried about the rise of robots coming for jobs but rarely did the reality match the concern. Then came ChatGPT, an AI chatbot that has gone viral, and it became the fastest-growing app with 100 million active users just two months after launching. Experts started to worry that the latest chatbots could jeopardize the careers of anyone who interprets information and generates written reports or commands. Chatbots can do very creative things that we previously thought were innately human, and an increasing number of users see this as a business opportunity. They will start using a chatbot as an additional staff member that may be compared to a newly hired graduate in terms of its ability to research and think. AI is much quicker and reliable, without needing a break or pension, and for business people, it’s vital. Some UK law firms are already using chatbots to draft legal letters or to come up with arguments in court cases. They are using chatbots as a kind of outsourced brain to reduce the workload on themselves. Difficult words: jeopardize (to expose to danger or risk), innately (naturally), outsourced (obtained by contract from an outside supplier). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

For many years, people worried that one day, robots could take their jobs. Now, it seems that it may start happening. ChatGPT is an AI chatbot, which is the fastest-growing app. It had 100 million active users only two months after launching . Chatbots are very creative, and they can do things, which we thought only people could do. Chatbots can work with information, do research, and write reports or commands . Some companies already realize this, and they start using chatbots. Chatbots work very fast and they don’t need a break. Some UK law companies already use chatbots to write legal letters or come up with arguments in legal cases, which means less work for the staff. Difficult words: launch (to start an activity or business), command (an order which tells someone what to do), argument (a reason or view which supports an idea). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

People always worry that robots will take their jobs. It seems that it is happening now. ChatGPT is an AI chatbot . It is quite a new app. But it quickly becomes popular. 100 million people use it two months after its start. They can chat with it. Chatbot talks with them about anything. Chatbots can work with information. They do research and write reports. They are very creative , too. Some companies already use chatbots for work. They work fast. They do not need a break. Chatbots write legal letters for some UK legal companies. This saves work for people. And companies save money. Difficult words: AI chatbot (a computer program which has a conversation with the person who uses it), research (a deep study of a subject), creative (someone who can think of many new ideas). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

TikTok’s recommendation algorithm has once again come under the spotlight while the US pressures TikTok’s Chinese owner ByteDance to sell the app’s US assets or face a nationwide ban. This algorithm is vital to ByteDance’s operations and is complex due to China’s export laws. Unlike its rivals, TikTok’s algorithm focuses on user interests rather than social connections, which enhances its effectiveness. The short video format allows for faster data collection and dynamic content exploration. This sets TikTok apart . TikTok also encourages users to form public groups, aiding in understanding user behavior and interests. Originating from Douyin, its Chinese counterpart, TikTok’s algorithm benefited from China’s low labor costs for content annotation . Difficult words: spotlight (when something is thoroughly examined by journalists and the public), set apart (to make someone seem distinctive or superior), annotation (adding notes or labels). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

TikTok’s special technology is its recommendation system . It makes it different from other apps. TikTok’s algorithm suggests videos based on what you like, not just who you know. This makes TikTok popular worldwide. Its short videos help the algorithm learn faster about what you like. TikTok also helps users find new things, not just what they already like. This technology started with a Chinese app called Douyin and got better with time. ByteDance is TikTok’s Chinese owner. China’s rules made it tricky to sell the app in the US. Now, US officials are pressuring ByteDance to sell the app’s US assets . If ByteDance doesn’t do it, officials may ban TikTok in the US. Difficult words: recommendation system (a tool which suggests videos), algorithm (a program which suggests content), asset (a thing which a person or company owns). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

TikTok has a special thing called a recommendation system. It suggests videos based on what you like. This makes TikTok different. TikTok is popular all over the world. It shows videos which people like. TikTok learns fast from short videos about what you like. TikTok also helps you find new things you may like. This special thing starts with Douyin, a Chinese app. But these days, TikTok knows much better what users like to watch. ByteDance owns TikTok. It is a Chinese company. China makes tricky rules about TikTok. Now, US officials ask ByteDance to sell its assets . If ByteDance does not do it, it may end in the US. Difficult words: based on (to use an idea or situation as the point from which you develop something), user (a person who uses something), asset (a thing which belongs to a person or company). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the UK, a trial for the first personalized vaccine against deadly melanoma is ongoing. This mRNA vaccine helps the immune system target and eliminate cancerous melanoma cells. What makes this vaccine unique is its personalized nature. It is tailored to each patient and matches their tumor’s genetic signature. The vaccine stimulates the body to produce proteins and antibodies that attack specific cancer cell markers and offers hope for reducing the risk of cancer recurrence . Similar trials are underway in Australia and other countries. The vaccine utilizes mRNA technology like some COVID vaccines. If the trial is successful, it could potentially extend to treating other types of cancers such as lung, bladder, and kidney cancers. Difficult words: melanoma (skin cancer), mRNA (a type of genetic material), recurrence (return of a disease). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the UK, scientists are testing a new vaccine for melanoma, a deadly skin cancer. This vaccine is special because it is just for each person. It matches each person’s genetic information. It teaches the immune system to find and destroy dangerous cancer cells . The vaccine makes the body produce proteins and antibodies which fight the cells. Similar tests are happening in Australia and other countries. The vaccine may help other cancers too, for example, lung, bladder, and kidney cancer. People hope it stops cancer from coming back. If the test is successful and it works, it could help people all over the world. Difficult words: deadly (a disease which can kill you), cell (the smallest part of a living organism), antibody (a foreign substance which gets in your body). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In the UK, scientists are testing a new vaccine. The vaccine is for melanoma. Melanoma is skin cancer . It is very dangerous. It kills thousands of people every year. This vaccine is special. It is different for every person. It works with the immune system . It helps the body find and fight dangerous cells . Similar tests are happening in Australia and other countries too. People hope that it will work. It may stop cancer from coming back. If it works, it can save people in the world. Difficult words: cancer (a dangerous disease when a part of the body starts to grow without control), immune system (organs and substances in the body which make the body strong), cell (the smallest part of a living organism). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The wings of the legendary cabaret in Paris’s Montmartre fell off and damaged the tourist attraction’s facade. Authorities reported no injuries and assured no further risk of collapse. The venue’s management ruled out vandalism and attributed the incident to a technical problem. The fallen blades caused damage to the building’s front and removed the letters ‘MOU’ from the illuminated sign. According to Moulin Rouge director general Jean-Victor Clerico, the blades will be put back in place soon, and shows at the venue will continue without cancellation. Established in 1889, the Moulin Rouge is one of the world’s most famous cabaret clubs. The current windmill was built in the 1920s. The only major incident in the Moulin Rouge’s history was a fire in 1915 that led to its closure for nine years. The cabaret symbolizes Parisian nightlife and is renowned for its French cancan dance. It’ll mark its 135th anniversary on October 6 this year. Difficult words: legendary (very well known), cabaret (entertainment held in a nightclub or restaurant while the audience eats or drinks at tables), vandalism (intentional damage to property). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Last week, the windmill sails of Paris’s famous Moulin Rouge cabaret fell off and damaged the building’s front. Nobody got hurt and there was no other danger. Moulin Rouge’s director said that they would repair the mill soon and shows will continue without a break. He added that the accident happened because of technical problems and it was not vandalism . The Moulin Rouge is one of the most famous cabaret clubs in the world. This year, it will be 135 years since its opening. This symbol of Paris nightlife is popular for its French cancan dance. Difficult words: windmill (a building with sails which turn in the wind and make power), cabaret (a show at a nightclub or restaurant), vandalism (breaking things on purpose). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The windmill of Moulin Rouge is a famous place in Montmartre, Paris. Last week, its sails fall off. The sails damage the front of the building. Letters M, O, and U fall off the sign. Luckily, nobody is hurt. It is a technical problem. The director says that new sails will be ready soon. The shows do not stop. Moulin Rouge is a famous cabaret . It is a place for shows and dancing. It starts in 1889. This year, the place celebrates 135 years. People can see there the famous French cancan dance. Difficult words: windmill (a building with a sail which turns in the wind and makes power), technical (related to machines or science), cabaret (a show at a nightclub or restaurant). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Brazil is witnessing a surge in land protests that mark the 40th anniversary of its agrarian reform movement. The Landless Workers Movement has organized 30 land occupations across 13 states. They demand enforcement of their rights under Brazil’s constitution, which mandates the redistribution of unproductive land to people in need. The government promised to settle 73,000 families with a 100-million-dollar investment; however, activists argue it is insufficient. The farm lobby has a big influence in Congress. It opposes squatters and pushes for laws to expel them without going to court. Some people believe Brazil can accommodate both the rich and poor. Advocates draw from their own experience of transitioning from a camp to a sustainable livelihood. The protests often turn violent, especially in remote regions of the Amazon rainforest. At least 1,690 violent clashes over land took place in Brazil last year, according to a recent report. Difficult words: mandate (to give someone authority to act in a certain way), lobby (a group of people who seek influence on politicians on a particular issue), squatter (a person who illegally occupies an inhabited building or unused land). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

40 years after agrarian reform, Brazil experiences many protests. The Landless Workers Movement is organizing these protests. According to Brazil’s law, the country has to ensure food security . The movement asks the government to give land to people who need it so that they can grow food. The government promised to settle 73,000 families with 100 million dollars, but it is not enough. Some families use land illegally. The farm lobby has big power and they want these people to leave without going to court. Activists believe that there is enough land for both the rich and the poor. In the meantime, the protests continue. Almost 1,700 protests took place last year, many of them in the Amazon rainforest. Difficult words: agrarian (related to farming), food security (when all people have enough food), settle (to give money to someone), lobby (a group of people who influence politicians). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Brazil, there are protests about land. People want the land to grow food. A group of people is organizing these protests. They say the government must give land to people who need it. The government promises to help. The government will give 100 million dollars to 73,000 families. But it is not enough. The farm lobby does not agree with the protesters. They want laws to remove protesters. Some people think that there is food for everyone. One woman lives in a camp in the past. But now she sells fruits and vegetables. She believes that there is enough land for both rich and poor people. Difficult words: lobby (people who have big power and they change politics), law (an official rule), remove (to take away). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

A very unusual incident happened in central London on Wednesday morning. Noise from builders near Buckingham Palace caused the military horses from the Household Cavalry to bolt during a rehearsal . According to the Army spokesman, five horses ran loose and four soldiers were unseated. The animals collided with traffic in several locations and some ran as far as Limehouse in east London, eight kilometers away from where the incident occurred. The quick reaction of emergency service providers enabled quick treatment of the injured soldiers and horses. All five horses were recovered; however, official didn’t provide information about their condition. Difficult words: bolt (to run away suddenly), rehearsal (a session of exercise or practice in preparation for a public performance). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Military horses ran through central London on Wednesday morning. The event caused chaos in the streets of Britain’s capital city. The horses ran away due to noise from builders near Buckingham Palace. Five horses escaped, and four soldiers fell off. Several people and horses were hurt. At least four people ended up in hospital. The horses collided with cars and buses, a tour bus ended up with a damaged windscreen . Two horses ran as far as Limehouse, eight kilometers from Buckingham Palace. Thanks to the quick reaction of emergency services, nothing serious happens. Difficult words: chaos (a situation when nobody knows what to do), collide (to crash), windscreen (the front window of a vehicle). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Something very unusual happens in London last week. Soldiers’ horses near Buckingham Palace have an exercise . Builders are nearby. They make a loud noise. The noise scares the horses. They run away. Four soldiers fall off them. Five horses run through central London. They crash with cars and buses. Several people are hurt. They must go to hospital. The horses are hurt too. Two horses run to Limehouse. Limehouse is eight kilometers from Buckingham Palace. Emergency services quickly solve the situation. All horses are better now. Difficult words: exercise (a physical activity, training), scare (to make someone afraid), fall off (to fall to the ground). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Europe’s fruit farmers are concerned about their harvests due to unexpected frosts during spring. The cold weather has led to worries about the food supply in Europe. Balkan countries have experienced a sudden drop in temperatures, causing snow and ice. Fruit farmers in Croatia and Poland have suffered losses due to the frost, with temperatures reaching as low as -8 degrees Celsius in some areas. However, Dutch farmers have found a solution by spraying water on their fruit trees, which creates a protective layer of ice that helps keep the buds warm. Despite these efforts, heavy snowfalls in higher altitudes have caused challenges for drivers. Forecasters expect these extreme conditions to continue all week. Difficult words: bud (a small part of a plant that develops into a flower or leaf), altitude (the height above sea level). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Fruit farmers in Europe worry about their harvests because of unexpected frost during spring. The cold weather caused concerns if there would be enough food in Europe. In Balkan countries, a sudden drop in temperatures brought snow and ice. The frost damaged fruit trees in Croatia and Poland. Temperatures were as low as -8 degrees Celsius. Dutch farmers found a clever way of protecting their fruit trees. They sprayed them with water which froze, and the ice kept the buds warm. Experts say that these extreme conditions may continue all week. Difficult words: harvest (what farmers grow in fields for food), unexpected (when you don’t think that something will happen), bud (a small part of a plant). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Fruit farmers in Europe worry. The weather is colder than usual. There is snow and ice. Farmers in Croatia and Poland lose fruit because of the cold. Temperatures reach -8 degrees Celsius. Balkan countries have the same problem. There is snow and ice. Farmers in the Netherlands find a clever way to protect their fruit. They sprayed water on the trees. The ice keeps the trees warm. Weather experts say that it will be cold all week. Europe may have problems with food this year. Difficult words: temperature (how cold or warm something is), protect (to keep safe). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

After a long delay, the US Congress finally passed a significant foreign aid package. This package totals 95 billion dollars, and it includes crucial support for Ukraine, Israel, Taiwan, and US partners in the Indo-Pacific region. The Senate and House of Representatives approved four bills, combining them into one comprehensive package. President Biden is set to sign it into law. The aid for Ukraine totals 61 billion dollars, and it aims to address urgent military needs. Ukrainian President Zelenskiy expressed gratitude for this vital support. Additionally, the package includes funds to counter China’s influence in the Indo-Pacific. Despite some opposition, bipartisan leaders stress the importance of supporting Ukraine and other allies in the face of Russian aggression and other global threats. Difficult words: comprehensive (including everything necessary), counter (to react with an opposing opinion or action, to defend), bipartisan (involving the cooperation of two political parties that usually oppose each other’s policies). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

The US Congress finally passed a large aid package for countries like Ukraine, Israel, and Taiwan. The total amount is 95 billion dollars, and it will help solve these nations’ problems. After months of delay, both the Senate and the House of Representatives agreed on four bills . They put them into one big package. US President Joe Biden will sign it into law soon. The help includes military support for Ukraine and money to fight against China’s power in the Indo-Pacific region. Although politicians didn’t agree on all things, they all said that it was important to support their friends and democracy . Difficult words: aid package (money, things, or services sent to other countries or organizations as a form of help), bill (an idea which a parliament talks about and can make a law), democracy (a system of government in which elected people are at power). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The US government speaks about more help to Ukraine, Israel, and Taiwan. It is not an easy talk. It takes longer than everyone thinks. Finally, US politicians agree to help. The president will sign it soon. The help is for things like guns and money for Ukraine. All help is 95 billion dollars. Ukraine will get 61 billion dollars. Leaders say that it is important to help friends. The US wants to help democracy and peace . Difficult words: sign (to write a name on an official document), democracy (a way of government where people choose their leaders), peace (the time without a war). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dams in Central Asia that hold uranium mine waste pose a severe risk due to instability caused by a 2017 landslide. The area near the town of Male was one of the world’s biggest uranium ore dumps developed by the Soviet Union between the 1940s and 1960s. Studies show that these dams which contain around 700,000 cubic meters of waste could collapse, which would lead to a Chernobyl-scale disaster. Such an event could contaminate water used for irrigation . This would affect millions of people in Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan. European efforts suggest that moving the waste away from the Mailuu-Suu River is necessary. This area, with 16 million residents, relies heavily on agriculture; however, the whole area is prone to earthquakes. The cost to relocate the waste is estimated at 22-25 million euros, aiming to prevent a catastrophic environmental crisis. Difficult words: pose (to present a problem or danger), irrigation (the supply of water to land or crops to help growth), prone (to be likely to be affected by something). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In Central Asia, there are dams which hold uranium mine waste . After a 2017 landslide, the area became unstable. There is a risk that these dams could collapse. There are often earthquakes in this area, which worries scientists. If these dams collapse, it could lead to a big disaster similar to Chernobyl. This disaster would affect water which farmers use for their fields. It would have an impact on 16 million people in Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan, who depend on farming. European experts suggest moving the waste away from the Mailuu-Suu River. They estimate that it would cost 22-25 million euros to do it. But it is necessary to prevent a big catastrophe . Difficult words: mine waste (unused things which come from taking minerals from the ground), estimate (to say what could be the cost, size, or value of something), catastrophe (an event which causes a lot of damage and hurts many people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Central Asia, there are dams full of dangerous waste . This waste comes from uranium mines. In 2017, there is an earthquake. The area is not stable anymore. The dams may break. If it happens, it will be a disaster as big as Chernobyl. Rivers are near the dams. Millions of people use water from these rivers. Farmers need it for their fields. A disaster would hurt Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, and Tajikistan. 16 million people live there. European experts want to move the waste away. It will cost 22-25 million euros. Difficult words: dam (a high wall across a river which holds water), waste (things or materials which people do not need and throw away), disaster (a serious event which hurts many people). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In Spain’s Canary Islands, thousands of people have protested against mass tourism. Protesters claim it’s overwhelming the islands. They’re calling for limits on tourist numbers and controls on what they see as harmful development. Despite this, they emphasize they’re not against tourism altogether, which is a significant part of the islands’ economy. Last year, 13.9 million tourists visited, six times more than the local population. The UK and Germany are the main markets. Protesters in the capital, Santa Cruz de Tenerife, held signs demanding respect for their land and limits on tourism. They’re frustrated that politicians prioritize building tourist complexes over residents’ needs. Similar protests occurred in mainland Spain. Activists are advocating for a sustainable tourism model considering environmental impacts and social issues like poverty. Difficult words: prioritize (to give a high priority to), advocate (to publicly support or recommend). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In the Canary Islands, many people protested against mass tourism. They believe that it is causing problems. They want to limit the number of tourists and control harmful development. Local people support tourism, but they feel that it is damaging their land and lives. Protesters are upset that politicians prioritize building hotels over local needs. Last year, the islands received 13.9 million tourists, which was six times more than the local population. Most tourists come from the UK and Germany. Similar protests took place in mainland Spain. People say that it is necessary to think about the natural world and the social problems which tourism brings. Difficult words: limit (to state the highest possible number, amount, and so on), prioritize (to make something more important than other things), social (relating to people as a group). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Many people in the Canary Islands protest. They say that there are too many tourists. Officials must say how many tourists can come. Too many people hurt the natural world. It has also a bad impact on local people. Tourism is hurting their land and lives. 13.9 million tourists come to the islands last year. It is six times more than local people. Most tourists come from the UK and Germany. People are upset . Officials care more about building hotels than helping local people. Similar protests happen in mainland Spain. Tourism must not hurt nature and poor people. Difficult words: local (people who live in a place), upset (angry and unhappy), mainland (a large piece of land, not an island). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dubai International Airport, one of the world’s busiest travel hubs, reopened partially after heavy flooding shut it down due to a record-breaking storm in the United Arab Emirates. The storm brought unprecedented rainfall, caused extensive damage, and claimed at least one life. Streets in Dubai resembled rivers as torrential rain overwhelmed the city and halted its financial activities. The immediate threat of the storm passed; however, the airport still faced challenges. Grounded jets occupied much of the available space which led to delays and overcrowding in terminals as stranded passengers wanted to rebook canceled flights. Experts suggest that while the role of climate change in this extreme weather event is not entirely clear, such incidents may become more frequent as global temperatures rise. Despite efforts like cloud seeding, the intensity of this rainfall indicates that people need to take broader climate adaptation measures. Difficult words: unprecedented (never seen or done before), resemble (to be like or similar to someone or something), adaptation (adjustment or change to cope with the new condition). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Dubai International Airport is one of the busiest airports in the world. Last week, a big storm brought torrential rain to the United Arab Emirates and flooded the airport. In one day, there was more rain than in the whole year. The rain damaged many things and even caused one person to die. The streets in Dubai looked like rivers because of all the water. The airport still had problems after the rain stopped. Many planes were on the ground, so there was not enough space. Lots of people got stuck at the airport because the airport canceled flights. Experts say that as the world gets warmer, we might see more big storms like this one, even in places where rain is not usual at all. Difficult words: torrential rain (very heavy rain), stuck (not able to move from a place or position). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Dubai Airport is a busy place. It is one of the biggest airports in the world. Last week, heavy rain hits the United Arab Emirates and Oman. Rain is not usual in these countries at all. In one day, there is more rain than in the whole year. The rain damages things. One person is dead. The streets in Dubai look like rivers. The airport cancels flights. Many people must stay at the airport. They cannot leave. Experts are not sure what causes the rain. But such things may happen more often in the future . Even in places with very little rain. Difficult words: damage (to hurt), cause (to make something happen), future (time ahead). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China’s economy outperformed predictions and it grew by 5.3% in early 2024, thanks to its emphasis on green manufacturing. Investments in advanced products like electric vehicles, batteries, and solar panels have been boosted thanks to high demand worldwide. However, this success has led to tensions with the West. Reliance on Chinese technology is crucial for achieving environmental goals. The US and EU claim China unfairly supports its industries and floods markets with affordable green goods. This situation raises concerns about fair competition and trade practices. In China, the economic shift has left some workers struggling to find new jobs. As China’s influence in green technology grows, the global community faces challenges in balancing economic growth with environmental sustainability. Difficult words: outperform (to perform or do better than someone or something), fair competition (competition based on quality, price, and services rather than unfair practices), balance (to compare the value of one thing with another). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

In 2024, China’s economy grew by 5.3% which was more than anyone expected. The main reason is that China focused on making green products like electric cars, batteries, and solar panels. Other countries worry about relying too much on these items from China. They say that China supports its companies too much, which makes their products too cheap and hurts other businesses. This tension between China and other countries could cause problems. China’s success in green technology is changing the world, but it also brings challenges for everyone to work together fairly. Also, these changes mean that some people in China lost their jobs and can’t find new ones. Difficult words: focus (to be very interested in something), rely (to depend on), tension (stress or problems between people or countries). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

China’s economy grows a lot in 2024. Chinese companies start making green things like electric cars, batteries, and solar panels. But other countries worry. They need China and its products. They depend on China too much. But they think that China helps its companies too much. It means that Chinese products are very cheap. It hurts businesses in other places. China is very good at producing green products. It is changing the world. The West is angry at China. It is changing the lives of people in China too. Many older workers lose their jobs. Companies make different products. They hire young workers. Difficult words: green (friendly to nature), hurt (to have a bad impact on), hire (to take on a person to work in a company). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The chief weapons handler responsible for loading a gun for actor Alec Baldwin, who accidentally fired and killed a cinematographer in 2021, has been sentenced to 18 months in prison. Hannah Gutierrez-Reed was found guilty of involuntary manslaughter in March for mistakenly loading a live round into the revolver used by Baldwin on the film set of ‘Rust’. ‘You were the armorer – the one responsible for ensuring the weapon’s safety, yet you turned it into a deadly weapon’, stated Judge Mary Marlowe Sommer during sentencing. Gutierrez-Reed’s punishment marks the most significant legal consequence so far in the aftermath of Hutchins’ death, a case that has garnered significant attention in Hollywood and across the US. Difficult words: live round (a real bullet fired from a gun), aftermath (the consequences of a significant unpleasant event), garner (to get or collect). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Hannah Gutierrez-Reed was in charge of handling guns during the making of the movie ‘Rust’. Sadly, actor Alec Baldwin accidentally shot and killed a cinematographer in March 2021. The judge found Gutierrez-Reed guilty of involuntary manslaughter because she loaded a real bullet into the gun that Baldwin used. The judge said that Gutierrez-Reed was responsible for making sure the gun was safe but failed. It ended in a tragic accident. This sentence is the most serious consequence so far. The case caught the attention of Hollywood and the US. Difficult words: involuntary manslaughter (when you kill someone but you don’t plan it), consequence (the result or impact of an action), attention (when many people are interested in something). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Hannah Gutierrez-Reed is the armorer of the ‘Rust’ film. She looks after guns while making the movie. In March 2021, she gives a gun to actor Alec Baldwin. But real bullets are in the gun. Baldwin shoots and kills a cinematographer . Gutierrez-Reed goes to prison for 18 months. The judge says that Gutierrez-Reed must make sure that the gun is safe. But it does not happen. She makes a mistake. And a person dies because of her mistake. Many people talk about the accident in Hollywood and the US. This sentence is the most serious result of the accident so far. Difficult words: armorer (a person who looks after guns), cinematographer (a person with the camera), sentence (what a judge decides). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

German Chancellor Olaf Scholz visited China amidst growing tension between Europe and Beijing. Following a meeting with Chinese Premier Li Qiang, it was highlighted that the economic interests of both countries are closely linked. President Xi Jinping warned against protectionist measures and he advocated for free trade. Last year, Germany adopted a strategy to reduce reliance on China. Scholz’s visit coincided with Iran’s attack on Israel, prompting him to call for restraint . He also addressed concerns about China’s support for Russia amid the Ukraine conflict. Germany is pragmatic in dealing with China, but real progress remains uncertain. Difficult words: protectionist (favoring the restriction of imports), coincide (to occur at the same time), restraint (self-control or moderate behavior), pragmatic (dealing with things sensibly and realistically). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Germany’s leader Olaf Scholz went to China when relations between Europe and Beijing were not very good. After meeting with China’s Premier, they talked about how both countries need to do business with each other. China’s President Xi Jinping warned against doing anything that could hurt trade between China and Germany. Germany made a plan last year to not rely too much on China. Scholz also talked about an attack on Israel by Iran, and he said that everyone should calm down . He also talked about the war in Ukraine. Scholz said that it is important to be practical when dealing with China, but it is not clear if things will get better. Difficult words: rely (to depend on), calm down (to become less angry, upset, or excited), practical (helpful and real). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Germany’s leader Olaf Scholz goes to China. Things are not good between Europe and China. Scholz and Chinese Premier Li Qiang talk about how both countries need each other. They do a lot of business together. China’s leader says that the business must continue . Last year, Germany makes a plan. The country does not want to depend too much on China. Scholz also talks about an attack on Israel by Iran. It is important to stay calm. He also talks about the war in Ukraine. Scholz says that it is important to be sensible with China. It is not clear if things will get better. Difficult words: continue (to not stop), depend (to need something or someone), sensible (when you understand a situation and react well to it). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

In South Korea’s capital, Seoul, commuters have been using the world’s first driverless night bus. Self-driving taxis are becoming more common; however, autonomous public transport in city centers is rare. Nick Marsh from BBC News took a late-night ride on the Seoul autonomous bus, where advanced technology worth millions cruises the streets. The bus operates smoothly, with a driver present for emergencies. The creators see it as a solution to Seoul’s transport issues, especially for late-night travelers. Despite South Korea’s investment in autonomous vehicles, challenges remain. The technology isn’t perfect, and factors like unpredictable weather and road conditions bring troubles. Driverless public transport is still limited and costly but it signals a potential future of efficient urban transport. Difficult words: autonomous (operating independently), advanced (modern and well developed), signal (to indicate or show). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Commuters in Seoul are using the world’s first driverless night bus. Self-driving taxis are not so unusual anymore, but autonomous public transport in city centers is a new thing. A BBC reporter took a late-night ride on the Seoul autonomous bus. The vehicle uses modern technology which costs millions. The bus operates smoothly, but a driver is present for emergencies. Some people believe that autonomous buses will solve problems with public transport in the city, especially for late-night travelers. South Korea spends a lot of money on autonomous vehicles, but there are still troubles with it. It is expensive and it is not possible to use it everywhere. Difficult words: commuter (a person who travels to work or school), autonomous (a vehicle or machine which works without people), present (when a person is at a place). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Seoul is the capital of South Korea. People are using special buses there. These buses do not need a driver. They are autonomous . They drive at night. A ride on this bus is smooth and safe. The driver is there. But he is not driving. He helps if something goes wrong. Some people believe that these buses can solve problems with transportation . But there are still problems. The technology is not perfect yet. South Korea spends a lot of money on this transport. It costs very much money and it is not ready for every place yet. Difficult words: autonomous (when a machine or vehicle works without people), smooth (working without troubles), transportation (moving things or people from one place to another). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

The Brooklyn Public Library launched an initiative called Books Unbanned to tackle book censorship issues in certain areas of the country. This initiative allows young people under the age of 18 across the country to access the library’s entire collection digitally. Since its introduction, four other libraries, including the Seattle Public Library, have adopted similar programs. Brooklyn and Seattle’s public libraries discovered that some students signed up for library cards because they lacked access to nearby libraries. Others joined because certain book titles they were interested in were censored in their area. In a survey, the libraries received thousands of responses that offered insight into the impact of censorship and limited library access on young Americans. Difficult words: entire (the whole), adopt (to take up or follow), lack (to be without). You can watch the video news lower on this page.

Books Unbanned started at the Brooklyn Public Library to help with book censorship in some areas of the United States. Now, young people under 18 in the whole country can use the library’s books online. Four other libraries, including one in Seattle, liked the idea and did the same thing. The libraries found out that some children wanted library cards because they didn’t have a library nearby. Others wanted books which were banned in their area. When the libraries asked why the children wanted library cards, they got lots of answers. They saw what young people thought about book censorship and about not having a library nearby. Difficult words: censorship (not letting people read certain books or watch certain movies), banned (officially stopped). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.

Books Unbanned is an idea which starts in the Brooklyn Public Library . It helps children read books online. In some US states, it is not possible to read some books. They are banned . But libraries let children younger than 18 years read these books online . Four libraries do it now. In some areas, children cannot go to a nearby library. It is good that they can read the books online. Libraries ask children and young people why they want to read online. They get many interesting answers. Now they know how children feel if they cannot borrow some books. Difficult words: library (a place where people borrow books and magazines), ban (to officially stop), online (on the internet). You can watch the original video in the Level 3 section.
